Timing:

The party arrives at the camp in the late morning. The meeting is called for late afternoon. This gives them roughly 4-6 hours to explore.

What They Can Do:

The party can move freely between the Goodman and Fleurite sections. They may speak with any NPC, observe camp conditions, and gather intel. The nobles are aware of their presence and will be sizing them up.

Intel Gathering Opportunities:

The Common Fire (Goodman Section):

Read Aloud: A ring of blackened stones holds a low fire, the smoke curling into a grey late-autumn sky. Around it, a dozen or so figures huddle on logs and upturned crates — threadbare coats drawn tight, hands outstretched toward the warmth. The ground is churned mud. Beyond them, the camp stretches in uneven rows: patched canvas tarps, lean-tos of salvaged timber, a few proper tents that stand out against the rest. The murmur of low conversation carries the scent of woodsmoke and damp wool.

Poorer exiles: Talk of Maxis's harsh segregation policies. Resentment simmers. Many lost family in the destruction. Some mutter that the nobles are no better than the Inquisitors, just wealthier.
DC 10 Persuasion/Investigation: Learn that several families have talked about leaving the camp entirely, heading south on their own.
DC 15: One old woman mentions that Marcus Leondis is a good man, "not like the others." She says he's been seen arguing with Maxis late at night.

Supply Tent (Aris's Domain):

Read Aloud: A large canvas pavilion stands apart from the sleeping tents, its sides staked tight against the wind. Inside, crates of dried goods are stacked against the walls — grain, salt pork, hardtack — each stack shorter than the last. A folding table sits at the center, an oil lamp and a heavy leather-bound ledger its only furnishings. Duchess Aris Placidia sits behind it, her indigo silk gown a stark contrast to the rough canvas around her. She looks up as you enter, her pen still touching the page.

DC 12 Perception: Aris's ledger is visible on her table. She tracks every scrap of food. The numbers are tight — they have perhaps two weeks of rations left before they need to trade or forage.
DC 15 Persuasion with Aris: She will mention, offhand, that she's heard rumors of farms to the south willing to trade, but she doesn't have the manpower to secure the route without Marcus's militia — and Tichon won't spare the soldiers for "merchant errands."
Aris's general demeanor: Polite but guarded. She measures every word. She will steer conversation toward practical matters and away from politics.

Militia Post (Marcus's Command):

Read Aloud: A cluster of smaller tents on the north edge of the Goodman camp, set apart from the civilian quarters. A rack of spears and a few rusted swords stand under a canvas awning. A handful of men in mismatched armor — some in dented breastplates, most in padded jacks — sit on crates or stand in loose formation, going through drills with the tired look of men who have been at it all morning. Marcus Leondis stands at the center of it all, his patched leather cuirass stained with sweat, barking corrections in a voice that carries.

DC 10: Marcus's militia is a motley crew. A few former guards, mostly civilians. They drill in the mornings. Morale is low but holding.
DC 15 with Marcus (privately): If the party gains his trust, he might admit he's worried about a split. "If Maxis pushes too hard, I can't hold the line. My people aren't soldiers. They're fathers and sons who want to live."
DC 12 Perception: The militia's weapons are a mix of salvaged city guard gear and improvised tools. Ammunition is scarce.

Nobles' Accommodations (Goodman Section):

Read Aloud: The noble quarter takes up as much ground as the commons — a dense cluster of perhaps thirty canvas pavilions set on a slight rise, drawing an already apparent line between those who had and those who had not. Three tents stand apart from the rest, larger and better appointed. The ground here is drier, trampled flat and strewn with straw. A well-worn carpet — salvaged, once fine — lies before the entrance of the largest tent. A servant ducks out carrying a basin of grey water. The smell of coffee drifts on the air, a luxury you have not smelled since leaving the city. Tichon's tent bears a small coat of arms stitched into the flap — a steel anvil crossed with a hammer. Maxis's tent is flanked by a pair of empty crates used as benches. Aris's is the quietest, its flaps tied shut.

General: The nobles keep separate quarters. Servants move between them. The camp knows to keep a respectful distance.
DC 12 Perception: The noble tents are noticeably better supplied — thicker canvas, more space, proper cots visible through open flaps. The disparity is not lost on the poorer exiles.
DC 15 Investigation/Stealth (if snooping): Near Maxis's tent, a crumpled letter lies half-buried in the mud. It appears to be a draft of a proposal — hand-written notes about establishing a "Commerce Council" with himself at its head, and a list of names of wealthy Goodman survivors he considers allies.
DC 14 Insight (observing the servants): The servants who work for the nobles are drawn from the poor sections of the camp. They move quickly, heads down. One mutters under their breath that "Lord Maxis sent for the girl again last night" — vague, but suggestive of something the nobles would not want discussed.

Lucindus Arellius (Hidden in the Fleurite Camp):

Read Aloud: In a far corner of the Fleurite camp, where the tents thin out and the ground slopes toward the treeline, an old elf sits on a fallen log. He is bundled in a heavy cloak despite the still air, his hands resting on a gnarled walking stick. His silver-white hair is thin and wispy, his face deeply lined. He does not look up as you approach, but his hands tighten on the stick.

Lucindus keeps a low profile, staying in a quiet corner of the Fleurite section. Jace knows he's here and can point the party to him if asked.

DC 10 Investigation/Persuasion: The party can find Lucindus if they know to look for him. He's a 835-year-old High Elf artisan, visibly older than most, keeping to himself.
DC 12 Persuasion with Lucindus: He will reluctantly share what he knows about the inflection point — the statue in Fleurite Castle, the Aeon Stone materials, the laborers who died or went mad. He's terrified of being found by the Inquisitors.
DC 15: He admits he can describe the statue's construction in detail. He knows where it is in the castle. He also knows it wasn't built for Malygos alone — "There's something else using it. Something older."

Fleurite Camp Center (Lower Camp):

Read Aloud: The Fleurite camp is smaller and more cramped than the Goodman section, the tents pressed closer together as if for warmth. A single fire pit burns at the center, ringed by families sharing what little they have. A young elf with quick hands sits at a folding table nearby, a pile of half-fletched arrows before him — Rinnald Octinabeus. He looks up with a tired but eager expression as you approach.

Rinnald Octinabeus: The youthful fletcher running the camp is eager and earnest. He will talk freely about the camp's daily struggles. He mentions that Jace has been receiving letters from inside Fleurite — Leggiat Maneau's information.
DC 10 Insight: Rinnald is young and idealistic. He believes Jace can pull this off. He's nervous about the meeting but puts on a brave face.
DC 12 Persuasion: Rinnald admits the Fleurite exiles are running low on arrows. He's been fletching what he can, but materials are scarce. If the party can source feathers or arrowheads, he'd be grateful.
Fleurite exiles' general mood: Wary, tired, but loyal to Jace. They remember the Inquisitors. They'd rather take their chances in the wilderness than go back.

The Path Between:

Read Aloud: A muddy trail winds downhill from the Goodman camp to the Fleurite section, churned by boots and wagon wheels. The ground is slick, the grass along its edges trampled flat. From the Goodman side, you can see the Fleurite tents below, clustered and low. From the Fleurite side, the Goodman camp looms above — larger, higher, drier. The path itself is empty as you approach, but the footprints tell a story of traffic that is careful, hesitant, and always uphill.

DC 12 Perception: The path is well-trodden but the Goodman exiles visibly avoid it. A Fleurite exile coming up the path is often met with cold stares.
DC 15: A Fleurite woman carrying water up the path mutters that the Goodman nobles treat them like servants. "We're not their maids. We're not their property. Jace will sort it out."

Jace (Privately, Before the Meeting):

Read Aloud: Jace leads you away from the central fire, to a quiet spot near the edge of the Fleurite camp. The tent canvas flaps behind him, his dark hair and beard catching the low autumn light. He checks over his shoulder once before he speaks, his voice low and direct.

Jace will take the party aside if they seek him out. He'll lay out his position honestly: he has no leverage. He's hoping the party's presence and their story from the mountains will buy him enough credibility to keep the nobles from demanding outright subjugation.
DC 12 Insight: Jace is more worried than he lets on. He's gambling everything on this meeting.
DC 15: He admits, quietly, that if the nobles force a merger on their terms, he'll have to flee with his people rather than submit. "I won't trade one tyrant for three."

Rumors & Camp Gossip (Random Encounters):

Roll or pick as the party moves through the camp:

1. A Goodman exile mutters that the nobles are hoarding the best rations for themselves.
2. A child points at Ruhrogue and asks if he's a "real hero from the mountains."
3. Two Goodman militiamen argue about whether to trust the Fleurite exiles.
4. An old Fleurite exile recognizes Ruhrogue's face but can't place it. (Potential trigger for the identity reveal if pursued.)

DC 15 with Marcus (privately): If the party gains his trust, he might admit he's worried about a split. "If Maxis pushes too hard, I can't hold the line. My people aren't soldiers. They're fathers and sons who want to live."
DC 12 Perception: The militia's weapons are a mix of salvaged city guard gear and improvised tools. Ammunition is scarce.

Nobles' Accommodations (Goodman Section):

Read Aloud: The noble quarter takes up as much ground as the commons — a dense cluster of perhaps thirty canvas pavilions set on a slight rise, drawing an already apparent line between those who had and those who had not. Three tents stand apart from the rest, larger and better appointed. The ground here is drier, trampled flat and strewn with straw. A well-worn carpet — salvaged, once fine — lies before the entrance of the largest tent. A servant ducks out carrying a basin of grey water. The smell of coffee drifts on the air, a luxury you have not smelled since leaving the city. Tichon's tent bears a small coat of arms stitched into the flap — a steel anvil crossed with a hammer. Maxis's tent is flanked by a pair of empty crates used as benches. Aris's is the quietest, its flaps tied shut.

General: The nobles keep separate quarters. Servants move between them. The camp knows to keep a respectful distance.
DC 12 Perception: The noble tents are noticeably better supplied — thicker canvas, more space, proper cots visible through open flaps. The disparity is not lost on the poorer exiles.
DC 15 Investigation/Stealth (if snooping): Near Maxis's tent, a crumpled letter lies half-buried in the mud. It appears to be a draft of a proposal — hand-written notes about establishing a "Commerce Council" with himself at its head, and a list of names of wealthy Goodman survivors he considers allies.
DC 14 Insight (observing the servants): The servants who work for the nobles are drawn from the poor sections of the camp. They move quickly, heads down. One mutters under their breath that "Lord Maxis sent for the girl again last night" — vague, but suggestive of something the nobles would not want discussed.

Lucindus Arellius (Hidden in the Fleurite Camp):

Read Aloud: In a far corner of the Fleurite camp, where the tents thin out and the ground slopes toward the treeline, an old elf sits on a fallen log. He is bundled in a heavy cloak despite the still air, his hands resting on a gnarled walking stick. His silver-white hair is thin and wispy, his face deeply lined. He does not look up as you approach, but his hands tighten on the stick.

Lucindus keeps a low profile, staying in a quiet corner of the Fleurite section. Jace knows he's here and can point the party to him if asked.

DC 10 Investigation/Persuasion: The party can find Lucindus if they know to look for him. He's a 835-year-old High Elf artisan, visibly older than most, keeping to himself.
DC 12 Persuasion with Lucindus: He will reluctantly share what he knows about the inflection point — the statue in Fleurite Castle, the Aeon Stone materials, the laborers who died or went mad. He's terrified of being found by the Inquisitors.
DC 15: He admits he can describe the statue's construction in detail. He knows where it is in the castle. He also knows it wasn't built for Malygos alone — "There's something else using it. Something older."

Fleurite Camp Center (Lower Camp):

Read Aloud: The Fleurite camp is smaller and more cramped than the Goodman section, the tents pressed closer together as if for warmth. A single fire pit burns at the center, ringed by families sharing what little they have. A young elf with quick hands sits at a folding table nearby, a pile of half-fletched arrows before him — Rinnald Octinabeus. He looks up with a tired but eager expression as you approach.

Rinnald Octinabeus: The youthful fletcher running the camp is eager and earnest. He will talk freely about the camp's daily struggles. He mentions that Jace has been receiving letters from inside Fleurite — Leggiat Maneau's information.
DC 10 Insight: Rinnald is young and idealistic. He believes Jace can pull this off. He's nervous about the meeting but puts on a brave face.
DC 12 Persuasion: Rinnald admits the Fleurite exiles are running low on arrows. He's been fletching what he can, but materials are scarce. If the party can source feathers or arrowheads, he'd be grateful.
Fleurite exiles' general mood: Wary, tired, but loyal to Jace. They remember the Inquisitors. They'd rather take their chances in the wilderness than go back.

The Path Between:

Read Aloud: A muddy trail winds downhill from the Goodman camp to the Fleurite section, churned by boots and wagon wheels. The ground is slick, the grass along its edges trampled flat. From the Goodman side, you can see the Fleurite tents below, clustered and low. From the Fleurite side, the Goodman camp looms above — larger, higher, drier. The path itself is empty as you approach, but the footprints tell a story of traffic that is careful, hesitant, and always uphill.

DC 12 Perception: The path is well-trodden but the Goodman exiles visibly avoid it. A Fleurite exile coming up the path is often met with cold stares.
DC 15: A Fleurite woman carrying water up the path mutters that the Goodman nobles treat them like servants. "We're not their maids. We're not their property. Jace will sort it out."

Jace (Privately, Before the Meeting):

Read Aloud: Jace leads you away from the central fire, to a quiet spot near the edge of the Fleurite camp. The tent canvas flaps behind him, his dark hair and beard catching the low autumn light. He checks over his shoulder once before he speaks, his voice low and direct.

Jace will take the party aside if they seek him out. He'll lay out his position honestly: he has no leverage. He's hoping the party's presence and their story from the mountains will buy him enough credibility to keep the nobles from demanding outright subjugation.
DC 12 Insight: Jace is more worried than he lets on. He's gambling everything on this meeting.
DC 15: He admits, quietly, that if the nobles force a merger on their terms, he'll have to flee with his people rather than submit. "I won't trade one tyrant for three."

Rumors & Camp Gossip (Random Encounters):

Roll or pick as the party moves through the camp:

1. A Goodman exile mutters that the nobles are hoarding the best rations for themselves.
2. A child points at Ruhrogue and asks if he's a "real hero from the mountains."
3. Two Goodman militiamen argue about whether to trust the Fleurite exiles.
4. An old Fleurite exile recognizes Ruhrogue's face but can't place it. (Potential trigger for the identity reveal if pursued.)
5. A merchant who fled Fleurite mentions that the Inquisitors have been quieter lately — "Like they're waiting for something."
6. A young Goodman exile quietly asks if the party has heard of a place called Unity. "I heard it's a city where everyone has a say. Is that true?"

Goodman City Exiles (Upper Camp):

The larger section, occupying the higher, drier ground. Refugees from Goodman's city since its destruction by Ishi'go'dan (~11/11/505). Organized around the pre-existing political structure of the city — the three surviving nobles (Tichon, Maxis, Aris) act as camp leaders.

Atmosphere: Tense, stratified. The wealthier exiles have proper tents, canvas walls, and furnishings salvaged from the city. The poorer exiles are in the lower end of this section with patched tarps, lean-tos, and shared blankets. A visible class divide.

Fighting force: ~150 troops (the Goodman Militia), commanded by Marcus Leondis.

Fleurite Exiles (Lower Camp):

The smaller section, set slightly downhill. Refugees from Fleurite who fled the Inquisitors' rule. Led by Jace Valamacke. Day-to-day operations run by Rinnald Octinabeus.

Atmosphere: Bleaker, more cramped, but more communal. The Fleurite exiles share what they have. The mood is wary — they know they're outnumbered and out-positioned.

Fighting force: ~50 troops.

Arrival:

Read Aloud — Outside: As the late afternoon light fades, you are called to the Goodman Administration Tent. It sits at the east edge of the camp, a massive pavilion of heavy canvas, its peak rising a full ten feet above the surrounding tents. Before it, a large communal firepit roars — more for ceremony than warmth, throwing long shadows across the trampled ground. A handful of armed militiamen stand at loose attention near the entrance, their eyes tracking you as you approach. The tent flaps are tied open, revealing a warm orange glow from within.

Read Aloud — Inside: The pavilion is spacious, the canvas walls braced with salvaged timber poles. A long table of dark, scarred wood dominates the center — heavy enough to have been a merchant's counter in another life. Mismatched chairs surround it: a high-backed armchair at the head, a few upholstered seats, the rest simple wooden stools. An oil lamp hangs from the center pole, casting a warm, uneven light. The ground is covered with a threadbare rug, its pattern faded but once fine. The air smells of lamp oil, canvas, and woodsmoke from the fire outside.

Read Aloud — The Attendees: The three nobles are already seated. Tichon Darelius stands behind his chair rather than sitting, his arms crossed, his steel-grey hair catching the lamplight. He wears a dark wool greatcoat over a high-collared tunic, his brass buttons dull but polished. Across from him, Lord Maxis Fontides sits with perfect posture, one hand resting on the table, his burgundy velvet coat immaculate, his silver-white hair oiled and swept back. He regards you with the faintest smile, as if you are an amusing distraction. At the far end, Duchess Aris Placidia sits with her ledger closed before her, her indigo silk gown the only color in the room, her silver-streaked hair braided tight. She watches you enter but says nothing.

Near the tent wall, apart from the nobles, Marcus Leondis stands in his patched leather cuirass, his tarnished brass badge catching the light. He nods once in your direction — a gesture of recognition, not deference.

Attendees:

Jace Valamacke — Host, Fleurite Exile leader — Liberate Fleurite from Inquisitors, free King Peter, peace treaty with Goodman exiles
Count Tichon Darelius — Steel Baron, Goodman camp co-leader — Separate settlement — Goodman exiles create their own
Lord Maxis Fontides — Mill Baron, Goodman camp co-leader — Dominant commerce sector in Fleurite, equal to the crown
Duchess Aris Placidia — Silk Baron, Goodman camp co-leader — Neutral — wants wealth/status back, leans alliance with Fleurite but distrusts them
Marcus Leondis — Goodman Militia commander — Wants dissolution of monarchy and oligarchy, favors Unity-style democracy (won't say this openly)
Vika Lana — Forest elf, independent — Wants to focus on the global Romulus problem
The Party — — — Unknown

Likely Flow:

1. Jace opens with the proposal: destroy the Inquisitors, free King Peter, negotiate peace.
2. Each noble stakes their position.
3. Marcus stays quiet unless drawn out.
4. Vika redirects toward the larger Romulus threat.
5. Party navigates between these factions.

Key Tensions:

Ruhrogue's identity as one of Goodman's assassins is unknown to the nobles. If revealed, it would disturb the peace.
The Goodman nobles assume the party are "poors" — reduces their perceived worth.
Fleurite exiles have only ~50 troops vs. ~150 Goodman militia. Jace has little leverage.
Jace has been stalling merger by exaggerating the party's importance from their mountain expedition.
The party's actual accomplishments exceed Jace's claims. If the party tells their own story well, it validates Jace's bluff. If they downplay it or fail to impress, Jace loses credibility.

What the Party Knows (From Legwork):

If the party did their legwork, they should have:
Aris's position — she's the most persuadable, but she needs to see a path to regaining her wealth.
Maxis's ambition — he wants power, not just survival. He can be bought with a position.
Tichon's stubbornness — he wants separation. He won't be moved easily.
Marcus's hidden sympathies — he's an ally in waiting, but he won't act openly.
The rations crisis — the camp can't sustain itself indefinitely. This is a lever.
The militia's weakness — the Goodman fighting force is fragile. Morale is low.

Contingencies:

If Ruhrogue's identity is revealed: Immediate crisis. The nobles may demand justice or attack. Aris may be the most likely to demand a trial rather than violence.
If the party brokers a deal: Determine what each faction is willing to concede.
If Jace's bluff is called: The nobles demand to know what the party actually accomplished. Low rolls on the party's recounting will weaken Jace's position. High rolls with the NPCs they've cultivated will strengthen it.
If the party ignores legwork: The nobles will be more dismissive. The party will have less to work with at the table.

Possible Outcomes:

Alliance: The camps unite under a joint command. The nobles accept Jace's proposal with conditions.
Separation: Tichon wins. The camps remain separate but agree to mutual defense.
Subjugation: Maxis wins. The Fleurite exiles become subservient to the Goodman nobles.
Stalemate: No agreement. The meeting ends with tensions higher than before.
Collapse: Ruhrogue's identity is revealed, or a deal is botched. The camps split violently.

In truth, ending mortality makes Myrin more like the Far Realm and prepares it for merger. Malygos does not understand the ley-line damage, the Far Realm's true goal, or that he is a lever rather than the architect; he is misled and acts from the belief that he is saving creation.

graph_sources.assertion: The inflection point takes the form of a statue that symbolically represents the Far Realm Entity — a hideous, corrupted male/female angel with ghastly proportions and tentacles. Romulus tells his followers it represents Lord Malygos. It is being constructed in the treasure room of Fleurite Castle. Only the Inquisitors and a handful of artisans know about it; most of those artisans have been murdered or driven insane.

A statue is being constructed in the treasure room — the inflection point for the Infinite Twilight. It is made from Aeon Stone material harvested from all four elemental planes, forming a hybrid crystal structure. The statue symbolically represents the Far Realm Entity (though Romulus tells followers it represents Malygos). Romulus pours psionic energy into it daily.

Only the Inquisitors and a handful of artisans know about it.
Most of the artisans who worked on it have been murdered or driven insane.

Romulus and his brother Rhetus were taken in by the priests of Malygos after their homeland was destroyed by war (~290CE). While Rhetus focused on the church, Romulus spent years corrupting the nobility of Fleurite.

Romulus was practically born to enact the Infinite Twilight. He had visions of it for decades before the priesthood of Malygos brought him in on their plan. The Far Realm Entity selected him as a child (~290CE) to serve as its Controlled Anchor on Myrin.

Following the death of the hero Ruh at "The Ocho," Romulus used his psionic powers to mentally dominate King Peter le Fleur, effectively ending the benevolent monarchy. He rebranded the White Cloaks into the Inquisitors and synthesized the Church's religious authority with the capitalist greed of Goodman's former city-state to fund his global expansion.

evidence.assertion:
Roccid is from the noble House Drusus. Their standing amongst the other noble houses had remained high for centuries. They were known as merchants and traders, responsible for much of the goods imported from Phyro and Bastok.

Two years ago, the climate of the city started to change. The King decreed that Fleurite was a Kingdom alone — no more trade with outside nations would be permitted. House Drusus could have stood on its substantial wealth, but rumors started to circulate that they weren't just tolerant of outsiders — they actively supported them. Members of House Drusus were said to have even married outsider peoples. It wasn't long before House Drusus was stripped of its nobility.

In an attempt to get back into the graces of the Kingdom, Roccid's parents sent him to the castle to train with the Assassins Guild. There he was indoctrinated into believing the many evils of outsiders and the wrongdoings of the past peoples of Fleurite. One such individual was Ruhrogue — a beloved disciple of the master Ruh, who viciously betrayed and murdered his master, then fled the city to live amongst the outsiders he was supporting.

Roccid was eventually sent to assassinate Ruhrogue. He failed and was mortally wounded by Ruhrogue in the encounter. Penelope, a member of Ruhrogue's party, found Roccid dying in an alley and healed him. Since then, Roccid sought out Ruhrogue and became his apprentice. He has grown disillusioned by Fleurite's current state and sees Ruhrogue as a possible solution to the corruption.

Roccid spent several days alone at the Monastery with Sorin while the party ascended Ishi'ra'la. They did not know each other much before, but have grown close. Both raised on stories of their people's good deeds, both disillusioned by Fleurite. They made a pact to support Ruhrogue in any attempt to repair the corruption in Fleurite.

evidence.assertion:
High elf woman with pale silver-blonde hair, light green eyes, and a composed, aristocratic bearing. Since settling in the exile camp, the refinement of Grey House has given way to practicality. She still keeps her hair carefully bound and her clothing orderly, but her once-fine white dresses are now repeatedly mended, dust-stained, and altered for daily work around the camp. A sturdy belt and worn shoes have replaced more ornamental accessories.

She refuses to look defeated. Even exhausted, Lily stands straight, keeps herself clean when circumstances allow, and carries herself with the deliberate dignity of someone determined not to let exile strip away who she is.

graph_sources.assertion:
Arrest:

Lady Lily Valamacke was arrested by the White Cloaks approximately two days before the dungeon incursion (late December 2025). Unlike Dariferra, who had been held for nearly a month and severely brutalized, Lily was kept physically unharmed. She was taken not for information or punishment, but as bait — the Inquisitors intended to draw the rebellion into the open.

Dungeon Incursion:

During the party's tunnel incursion into Castle Fleurite's dungeon, Lily was held in a cell along the upper right stretch of the main horizontal hallway. Hearing the noise of the incursion, she began calling out to rally other prisoners. When the party arrived, she immediately asked about Jace, demanded prisoners be freed, and pushed for action.

Once freed, she helped free numerous other prisoners — both rebels and civilians. Her actions significantly accelerated the breakdown of dungeon control during the escape.

Post-Escape:

After escaping through the tunnel back to Grey House, Lily and Jace quickly pieced together that the incursion had been too easy — she had never been meant to disappear long-term. The Inquisitors wanted names, faces, and a single place to point at and call treason.

As the rebels fled Grey House, Ishi'go'dan was forced by Romulus to destroy the manor with a lightning bolt.

Exile Camp:

The rebellion fled south and joined the Goodman City survivors' encampment. Lily and Jace have been keeping the peace between the Fleurite exiles and the Goodman City exiles — a tentative arrangement. She spoke alongside Jace about possibly working together to fight back against the Inquisitors.

Lily remains calm, intelligent, and sharply decisive, but life in the exile camp has made her more openly pragmatic. She spends much of her time resolving disputes, organizing necessities, and dealing with the mundane problems of keeping frightened and angry people together.

Her fury toward the Inquisitors has cooled from something immediate into something harder and more disciplined. She rarely raises her voice, but she has little patience for pointless arguments, old rivalries, or anyone jeopardizing the camp for pride.

Where Jace is increasingly consumed by the rebellion and what was taken from them, Lily has become the stabilizing force beside him. She reminds him that they are no longer simply fighting for Fleurite—they are responsible for the people who survived it.

She is courteous without being soft, compassionate without being sentimental, and increasingly comfortable exercising authority in her own right.

Pre-Rebellion:

Jace Valamacke was the lord of Grey House, his ancestral manor across the road from Castle Fleurite. He served as a court council to King Peter le Fleur before the Inquisitors' takeover.

The Rebellion:

When the Inquisitors under Romulus seized control of Fleurite, Jace became the leader of the rebellion. He established the Dirty Duckling tavern as the rebellion's secret meeting place, with innkeep Leggiat Maneau as his informant.

The Dungeon Incursion:

A tall, slender elf with dark hair, Jace was introduced to the players by Vika Lana at the Dirty Duckling. She vouched for them as heroes from the north, and Jace accepted them as allies — though his patience was thin. He revealed that his wife, Lady Lily Valamacke, had been arrested and taken to the dungeon under Castle Fleurite just two days prior, expediting his need for action.

The players and Jace agreed to join forces. Jace had started an underground tunnel from Grey House across the road from Castle Fleurite. Coreferra summoned 8 giant badgers to assist in digging. Through this tunnel, they entered the dungeon, freed Lily, Dariferra, and other prisoners.

After the escape, Jace and Lily realized the incursion was meant to be a trap for the rebellion. As they fled, Ishi'go'dan was forced by Romulus to destroy Grey House with a lightning bolt, obliterating it.

The Exile Camp:

The rebellion fled Fleurite and joined the exile camp south of the city. Jace and Lily have been keeping the peace between the Fleurite exiles and the Goodman City exiles, but it's been tentative. Leggiat Maneau continues to secrete information to Jace from within Fleurite.

Vika Lana — Old friend — Long familiarity; treats her like an old friend and trusts her judgment

graph_sources.assertion:
Purpose: Ishi'go'dan lays into the players for their "stupid, do-nothing" actions.

Key Slights He Attacks:

1. Lieutenant Deaths (if applicable):
If one or both lieutenants are dead: He's pissed. One exploding fueled the convergence core; the other fled. He sees this as incompetence, not victory.
Read-aloud: "How dare you kill my loyal, if not sullied, lieutenants. Disgusting mortals are not worth their weight in feathers. All you bring is destruction and evil."

2. Ruhrogue's Arrogance:
He can see it in Ruhrogue's smirk — represents the arrogance of mortals
Unwilling to humble himself before the glory and might of a Titan
He sees this as unjustified
Read-aloud: "Ishi'go'dan turns his ireful gaze on Ruhrogue. Look at that smirk. The arrogance. The sheer, unearned pride. Mortals think themselves so clever, so important. But you're nothing. You're dust that thinks it's kings."

3. Coreferra:
He knows Coreferra is the pathetic little peon Arkin sends to do his bidding
He sees Coreferra as yet another example of a god who won't act himself, sending mortals to do his dirty work
He's disgusted that Coreferra has the arrogance to be in his presence
Read-aloud: "His weight shifts and he snorts at Coreferra. The Hermit Monk sends his little pets to do his dirty work, and this one actually thinks he has a place here? A god who won't stand his own ground, relying on pathetic little mortals to face a Titan. Disgusting."

4. Ladir and the Aeon Stones:
He's furious that Ladir is lugging around aeon stones like they belong to him
He demands an explanation and will throw this at Ladir directly
Between Ladir and the stones, they'll have to convince him of their good intentions
Some amount of purpose for the air stone must be discussed
Read-aloud: "He jerks his raging eyes to Ladir. You carry them like they're your own. Like they belong to you. Aeon stones meant for gods, and you—just a mortal—who do you think you are? Claiming power you haven't earned, parading knowledge you don't deserve."

5. Vika Lana (Medallions):
He senses the Medallions of the Golden Dawn the players are carrying
He recognizes the name and knows they're Oracle-summoning artifacts
He questions why mortals are carrying artifacts meant for divine beings
He can smell Vika Lana's handiwork in their creation — mad that she's another fool mortal involving herself in the affairs of beings greater than her
Read-aloud: "Ishi'go'dan's entire body starts to vibrate like he's preparing to strike. He sneers at Vika Lana. filthy elves... of course. Another mortal who doesn't know her station. These artifacts are for Oracles, for divine beings. Who does she think she is—stirring up trouble, playing at power beyond her understanding? Another fool mortal thinking she can walk among titans and gods and not pay the price."

6. Zander's Tattoo:
He senses the binding magic on Zander's tattoo (not corruption)
Because it's similar to the magic used on him, he assumes Zander is with the Inquisitors
He may accuse Zander of working for his enemies
Read-aloud: "He raises an eyebrow, and with a sliver of concern stares at Zander. That mark... it's familiar. The binding magic. You think you can hide it? The Inquisitors think they can use you, use that seal, use me and my domain. Vile."

A dark suspicion seeps into his visage. These enemies... he mutters, they think they can walk in and make more demands of me. A Titan of the Sky. His entire body begins to vibrate, the sky above him cracking with dark energy. Lightning streaks through the air, and the sky itself screams in rage as he prepares to unleash devastation upon you.

Just as the storm reaches its peak, a flurry of crimson feathers streaks into view. A hawk explodes into the scene with impossible speed, flapping its wings and pecking at Ishi'go'dan's face—right between his eyes.

At first, the impossible serpent doesn't even notice. But as the realization dawns on him, his entire demeanor shifts. His face goes serene, gentle. He speaks to the hawk in a tender, fatherly tone: \"Hold on there, little aetherling. What's this about?\"
The hawk continues peck and claw at Ishi'go'dan's face for a moment, but then appears to finally notice the Titan waiting patiently. It starts squawking and chirping in petulant tones at Ishi'go'dan. Ishi'go'dan waits for the hawk to finish its tirade, and when it does, Ishi'go'dan's electric yellow eyes settle again on Zander. "Hmmmm" he says.

Dava flutters to Zander's shoulder. After a moment, a small voice — Endora's voice, carried by the Message spell — speaks directly into Zander's mind, crisp and clear amid the thunderous silence:

Read-aloud (Endora's message, via Dava): "Zander. It's me. Listen — I don't have long. I found something.

     "That mark on your arm — it's an abjuration symbol. A binding seal. I took it to Dean Kalandra at Unity, and she let me into the Abjuration archives. Your reputation opened that door, brother.

     "Inside, I found a report. Two thousand, two hundred years old. A village in Bastok — every person vanished overnight. Only one survivor. A man named Andice. Andice Thromius.

     "He had no memory of what happened. Badly wounded. But the Magister who found him sketched something in the report — a tattoo on his forearm. It's not identical to yours. But it's close. Too close to be coincidence.

     "And when I tried to dig deeper — I sent Dava to the archives in Gamorra — I got turned away. There's something called a 'Thromius Exemption' blocking the records. Our family name, Zander. Locking us out.

     "I think... I think you need to go home. Talk to Father. He knows more than he's ever told us.

     "I'll keep working from here. Stay safe."

The spell fades. Dava lets out a soft chirp and settles her feathers, cocking her head at Zander as if to say: _Well?_

Note to GM: This read-aloud dumps a lot of lore at once during a tense moment. Read it at a measured pace. The hawk's arrival defuses Ishi'go'dan's imminent attack, buying the party breathing room — but the tension hasn't gone anywhere. Ishi'go'dan is watching.

Tone: Hostile, condescending, suspicious. He doesn't trust mortals or gods.

Three-Pronged Counterstrike (post-Monastery):

After the party's escape from the Monastery, Romulus initiated three moves in parallel:
1. Send Ishi'go'dan east — Commanded the Titan to fly to the island of Mythis Minor and destroy the castle at Tsunadis, opening the door for the cultists summoning Ragga'na'ken.
2. Crack down on Fleurite peasants — A vindictive show of force, burning outer districts.
3. Send troops to wipe out the exile encampment — A preemptive strike against the rebellion before it can rally.

The Inflection Point:

Romulus constructed a massive ley-energy focus in the treasure room of Fleurite Castle — a statue built from Aeon Stone material connected to all four elemental domains. It serves as the reflecting point for the Infinite Twilight. He pours psionic energy into it daily. Only the Inquisitors and a handful of artisans know about it.

Final Campaign (Pre-Assault):

Before the party's assault on Fleurite, Romulus becomes openly consumed by power and paranoia:
Orders the Exile Camp destroyed.
Begins mass executions in Fleurite.
Sends Ishi'go'dan to support the cult at Mythis.

The players are vaguely aware that something is wrong with mortality or the divine order, but they do not know the Infinite Twilight's theology or name, or that Malygos is behind it. The Inquisitors and White Cloaks present themselves as correcting the world rather than destroying it.

Romulus and his brother Rhetus were taken in by the priests of Malygos after their homeland was destroyed by war (~290CE). While Rhetus focused on the church, Romulus spent years corrupting the nobility of Fleurite.

Romulus was practically born to enact the Infinite Twilight. He had visions of it for decades before the priesthood of Malygos brought him in on their plan. The Far Realm Entity selected him as a child (~290CE) to serve as its Controlled Anchor on Myrin.

Following the death of the hero Ruh at "The Ocho," Romulus used his psionic powers to mentally dominate King Peter le Fleur, effectively ending the benevolent monarchy. He rebranded the White Cloaks into the Inquisitors and synthesized the Church's religious authority with the capitalist greed of Goodman's former city-state to fund his global expansion.

graph_sources.assertion:
Arrest:

Lady Lily Valamacke was arrested by the White Cloaks approximately two days before the dungeon incursion (late December 2025). Unlike Dariferra, who had been held for nearly a month and severely brutalized, Lily was kept physically unharmed. She was taken not for information or punishment, but as bait — the Inquisitors intended to draw the rebellion into the open.

Dungeon Incursion:

During the party's tunnel incursion into Castle Fleurite's dungeon, Lily was held in a cell along the upper right stretch of the main horizontal hallway. Hearing the noise of the incursion, she began calling out to rally other prisoners. When the party arrived, she immediately asked about Jace, demanded prisoners be freed, and pushed for action.

Once freed, she helped free numerous other prisoners — both rebels and civilians. Her actions significantly accelerated the breakdown of dungeon control during the escape.

Post-Escape:

After escaping through the tunnel back to Grey House, Lily and Jace quickly pieced together that the incursion had been too easy — she had never been meant to disappear long-term. The Inquisitors wanted names, faces, and a single place to point at and call treason.

As the rebels fled Grey House, Ishi'go'dan was forced by Romulus to destroy the manor with a lightning bolt.

Exile Camp:

The rebellion fled south and joined the Goodman City survivors' encampment. Lily and Jace have been keeping the peace between the Fleurite exiles and the Goodman City exiles — a tentative arrangement. She spoke alongside Jace about possibly working together to fight back against the Inquisitors.

Goodman City Exiles (Upper Camp):

The larger section, occupying the higher, drier ground. Refugees from Goodman's city since its destruction by Ishi'go'dan (~11/11/505). Organized around the pre-existing political structure of the city — the three surviving nobles (Tichon, Maxis, Aris) act as camp leaders.

Atmosphere: Tense, stratified. The wealthier exiles have proper tents, canvas walls, and furnishings salvaged from the city. The poorer exiles are in the lower end of this section with patched tarps, lean-tos, and shared blankets. A visible class divide.

Fighting force: ~150 troops (the Goodman Militia), commanded by Marcus Leondis.

Fleurite Exiles (Lower Camp):

The smaller section, set slightly downhill. Refugees from Fleurite who fled the Inquisitors' rule. Led by Jace Valamacke. Day-to-day operations run by Rinnald Octinabeus.

Atmosphere: Bleaker, more cramped, but more communal. The Fleurite exiles share what they have. The mood is wary — they know they're outnumbered and out-positioned.

Fighting force: ~50 troops.

Pre-Rebellion:

Jace Valamacke was the lord of Grey House, his ancestral manor across the road from Castle Fleurite. He served as a court council to King Peter le Fleur before the Inquisitors' takeover.

The Rebellion:

When the Inquisitors under Romulus seized control of Fleurite, Jace became the leader of the rebellion. He established the Dirty Duckling tavern as the rebellion's secret meeting place, with innkeep Leggiat Maneau as his informant.

The Dungeon Incursion:

A tall, slender elf with dark hair, Jace was introduced to the players by Vika Lana at the Dirty Duckling. She vouched for them as heroes from the north, and Jace accepted them as allies — though his patience was thin. He revealed that his wife, Lady Lily Valamacke, had been arrested and taken to the dungeon under Castle Fleurite just two days prior, expediting his need for action.

The players and Jace agreed to join forces. Jace had started an underground tunnel from Grey House across the road from Castle Fleurite. Coreferra summoned 8 giant badgers to assist in digging. Through this tunnel, they entered the dungeon, freed Lily, Dariferra, and other prisoners.

After the escape, Jace and Lily realized the incursion was meant to be a trap for the rebellion. As they fled, Ishi'go'dan was forced by Romulus to destroy Grey House with a lightning bolt, obliterating it.

The Exile Camp:

The rebellion fled Fleurite and joined the exile camp south of the city. Jace and Lily have been keeping the peace between the Fleurite exiles and the Goodman City exiles, but it's been tentative. Leggiat Maneau continues to secrete information to Jace from within Fleurite.

evidence.assertion:
Goodman Administration Tent — Large canvas pavilion at the center of the Goodman section. Where camp meetings are held. Inside: a long wooden table (salvaged from the city), mismatched chairs, a single oil lamp.
The Common Fire — Central fire pit in the Goodman section. Gathering point for the poorer exiles. Good place to hear camp gossip.
Militia Post — A cluster of smaller tents near the north edge of the Goodman camp. Marcus Leondis's command post. Watch schedules posted, weapons stacked under canvas.
Supply Tent — Aris's domain. Rations are distributed here daily. A ledger is kept. She can be found here most mornings.
Fleurite Camp Center — A smaller gathering area with a single fire pit. Rinnald Octinabeus runs camp operations from a small folding table nearby.
The Path Between — The muddy trail connecting the two camps. The physical and social divide. Goodman exiles don't cross down often; Fleurite exiles climb up with caution.

graph_sources.assertion:
Timing:

The party arrives at the camp in the late morning. The meeting is called for late afternoon. This gives them roughly 4-6 hours to explore.

What They Can Do:

The party can move freely between the Goodman and Fleurite sections. They may speak with any NPC, observe camp conditions, and gather intel. The nobles are aware of their presence and will be sizing them up.

Intel Gathering Opportunities:

The Common Fire (Goodman Section):

Read Aloud: A ring of blackened stones holds a low fire, the smoke curling into a grey late-autumn sky. Around it, a dozen or so figures huddle on logs and upturned crates — threadbare coats drawn tight, hands outstretched toward the warmth. The ground is churned mud. Beyond them, the camp stretches in uneven rows: patched canvas tarps, lean-tos of salvaged timber, a few proper tents that stand out against the rest. The murmur of low conversation carries the scent of woodsmoke and damp wool.

Poorer exiles: Talk of Maxis's harsh segregation policies. Resentment simmers. Many lost family in the destruction. Some mutter that the nobles are no better than the Inquisitors, just wealthier.
DC 10 Persuasion/Investigation: Learn that several families have talked about leaving the camp entirely, heading south on their own.
DC 15: One old woman mentions that Marcus Leondis is a good man, "not like the others." She says he's been seen arguing with Maxis late at night.

Supply Tent (Aris's Domain):

Read Aloud: A large canvas pavilion stands apart from the sleeping tents, its sides staked tight against the wind. Inside, crates of dried goods are stacked against the walls — grain, salt pork, hardtack — each stack shorter than the last. A folding table sits at the center, an oil lamp and a heavy leather-bound ledger its only furnishings. Duchess Aris Placidia sits behind it, her indigo silk gown a stark contrast to the rough canvas around her. She looks up as you enter, her pen still touching the page.

DC 12 Perception: Aris's ledger is visible on her table. She tracks every scrap of food. The numbers are tight — they have perhaps two weeks of rations left before they need to trade or forage.
DC 15 Persuasion with Aris: She will mention, offhand, that she's heard rumors of farms to the south willing to trade, but she doesn't have the manpower to secure the route without Marcus's militia — and Tichon won't spare the soldiers for "merchant errands."
Aris's general demeanor: Polite but guarded. She measures every word. She will steer conversation toward practical matters and away from politics.

Militia Post (Marcus's Command):

Read Aloud: A cluster of smaller tents on the north edge of the Goodman camp, set apart from the civilian quarters. A rack of spears and a few rusted swords stand under a canvas awning. A handful of men in mismatched armor — some in dented breastplates, most in padded jacks — sit on crates or stand in loose formation, going through drills with the tired look of men who have been at it all morning. Marcus Leondis stands at the center of it all, his patched leather cuirass stained with sweat, barking corrections in a voice that carries.

DC 10: Marcus's militia is a motley crew. A few former guards, mostly civilians. They drill in the mornings. Morale is low but holding.
DC 15 with Marcus (privately): If the party gains his trust, he might admit he's worried about a split. "If Maxis pushes too hard, I can't hold the line. My people aren't soldiers. They're fathers and sons who want to live."
DC 12 Perception: The militia's weapons are a mix of salvaged city guard gear and improvised tools. Ammunition is scarce.

Nobles' Accommodations (Goodman Section):

Read Aloud: The noble quarter takes up as much ground as the commons — a dense cluster of perhaps thirty canvas pavilions set on a slight rise, drawing an already apparent line between those who had and those who had not. Three tents stand apart from the rest, larger and better appointed. The ground here is drier, trampled flat and strewn with straw. A well-worn carpet — salvaged, once fine — lies before the entrance of the largest tent. A servant ducks out carrying a basin of grey water. The smell of coffee drifts on the air, a luxury you have not smelled since leaving the city. Tichon's tent bears a small coat of arms stitched into the flap — a steel anvil crossed with a hammer. Maxis's tent is flanked by a pair of empty crates used as benches. Aris's is the quietest, its flaps tied shut.

General: The nobles keep separate quarters. Servants move between them. The camp knows to keep a respectful distance.
DC 12 Perception: The noble tents are noticeably better supplied — thicker canvas, more space, proper cots visible through open flaps. The disparity is not lost on the poorer exiles.
DC 15 Investigation/Stealth (if snooping): Near Maxis's tent, a crumpled letter lies half-buried in the mud. It appears to be a draft of a proposal — hand-written notes about establishing a "Commerce Council" with himself at its head, and a list of names of wealthy Goodman survivors he considers allies.
DC 14 Insight (observing the servants): The servants who work for the nobles are drawn from the poor sections of the camp. They move quickly, heads down. One mutters under their breath that "Lord Maxis sent for the girl again last night" — vague, but suggestive of something the nobles would not want discussed.

Lucindus Arellius (Hidden in the Fleurite Camp):

Read Aloud: In a far corner of the Fleurite camp, where the tents thin out and the ground slopes toward the treeline, an old elf sits on a fallen log. He is bundled in a heavy cloak despite the still air, his hands resting on a gnarled walking stick. His silver-white hair is thin and wispy, his face deeply lined. He does not look up as you approach, but his hands tighten on the stick.

Lucindus keeps a low profile, staying in a quiet corner of the Fleurite section. Jace knows he's here and can point the party to him if asked.

DC 10 Investigation/Persuasion: The party can find Lucindus if they know to look for him. He's a 835-year-old High Elf artisan, visibly older than most, keeping to himself.
DC 12 Persuasion with Lucindus: He will reluctantly share what he knows about the inflection point — the statue in Fleurite Castle, the Aeon Stone materials, the laborers who died or went mad. He's terrified of being found by the Inquisitors.
DC 15: He admits he can describe the statue's construction in detail. He knows where it is in the castle. He also knows it wasn't built for Malygos alone — "There's something else using it. Something older."

Fleurite Camp Center (Lower Camp):

Read Aloud: The Fleurite camp is smaller and more cramped than the Goodman section, the tents pressed closer together as if for warmth. A single fire pit burns at the center, ringed by families sharing what little they have. A young elf with quick hands sits at a folding table nearby, a pile of half-fletched arrows before him — Rinnald Octinabeus. He looks up with a tired but eager expression as you approach.

Rinnald Octinabeus: The youthful fletcher running the camp is eager and earnest. He will talk freely about the camp's daily struggles. He mentions that Jace has been receiving letters from inside Fleurite — Leggiat Maneau's information.
DC 10 Insight: Rinnald is young and idealistic. He believes Jace can pull this off. He's nervous about the meeting but puts on a brave face.
DC 12 Persuasion: Rinnald admits the Fleurite exiles are running low on arrows. He's been fletching what he can, but materials are scarce. If the party can source feathers or arrowheads, he'd be grateful.
Fleurite exiles' general mood: Wary, tired, but loyal to Jace. They remember the Inquisitors. They'd rather take their chances in the wilderness than go back.

The Path Between:

Read Aloud: A muddy trail winds downhill from the Goodman camp to the Fleurite section, churned by boots and wagon wheels. The ground is slick, the grass along its edges trampled flat. From the Goodman side, you can see the Fleurite tents below, clustered and low. From the Fleurite side, the Goodman camp looms above — larger, higher, drier. The path itself is empty as you approach, but the footprints tell a story of traffic that is careful, hesitant, and always uphill.

DC 12 Perception: The path is well-trodden but the Goodman exiles visibly avoid it. A Fleurite exile coming up the path is often met with cold stares.
DC 15: A Fleurite woman carrying water up the path mutters that the Goodman nobles treat them like servants. "We're not their maids. We're not their property. Jace will sort it out."

Jace (Privately, Before the Meeting):

Read Aloud: Jace leads you away from the central fire, to a quiet spot near the edge of the Fleurite camp. The tent canvas flaps behind him, his dark hair and beard catching the low autumn light. He checks over his shoulder once before he speaks, his voice low and direct.

Jace will take the party aside if they seek him out. He'll lay out his position honestly: he has no leverage. He's hoping the party's presence and their story from the mountains will buy him enough credibility to keep the nobles from demanding outright subjugation.
DC 12 Insight: Jace is more worried than he lets on. He's gambling everything on this meeting.
DC 15: He admits, quietly, that if the nobles force a merger on their terms, he'll have to flee with his people rather than submit. "I won't trade one tyrant for three."

Rumors & Camp Gossip (Random Encounters):

Roll or pick as the party moves through the camp:

1. A Goodman exile mutters that the nobles are hoarding the best rations for themselves.
2. A child points at Ruhrogue and asks if he's a "real hero from the mountains."
3. Two Goodman militiamen argue about whether to trust the Fleurite exiles.
4. An old Fleurite exile recognizes Ruhrogue's face but can't place it. (Potential trigger for the identity reveal if pursued.)
5. A merchant who fled Fleurite mentions that the Inquisitors have been quieter lately — "Like they're waiting for something."
6. A young Goodman exile quietly asks if the party has heard of a place called Unity. "I heard it's a city where everyone has a say. Is that true?"

Goodman City Exiles (Upper Camp):

The larger section, occupying the higher, drier ground. Refugees from Goodman's city since its destruction by Ishi'go'dan (~11/11/505). Organized around the pre-existing political structure of the city — the three surviving nobles (Tichon, Maxis, Aris) act as camp leaders.

Atmosphere: Tense, stratified. The wealthier exiles have proper tents, canvas walls, and furnishings salvaged from the city. The poorer exiles are in the lower end of this section with patched tarps, lean-tos, and shared blankets. A visible class divide.

Fighting force: ~150 troops (the Goodman Militia), commanded by Marcus Leondis.

Fleurite Exiles (Lower Camp):

The smaller section, set slightly downhill. Refugees from Fleurite who fled the Inquisitors' rule. Led by Jace Valamacke. Day-to-day operations run by Rinnald Octinabeus.

Atmosphere: Bleaker, more cramped, but more communal. The Fleurite exiles share what they have. The mood is wary — they know they're outnumbered and out-positioned.

Fighting force: ~50 troops.

Arrival:

Read Aloud — Outside: As the late afternoon light fades, you are called to the Goodman Administration Tent. It sits at the east edge of the camp, a massive pavilion of heavy canvas, its peak rising a full ten feet above the surrounding tents. Before it, a large communal firepit roars — more for ceremony than warmth, throwing long shadows across the trampled ground. A handful of armed militiamen stand at loose attention near the entrance, their eyes tracking you as you approach. The tent flaps are tied open, revealing a warm orange glow from within.

Read Aloud — Inside: The pavilion is spacious, the canvas walls braced with salvaged timber poles. A long table of dark, scarred wood dominates the center — heavy enough to have been a merchant's counter in another life. Mismatched chairs surround it: a high-backed armchair at the head, a few upholstered seats, the rest simple wooden stools. An oil lamp hangs from the center pole, casting a warm, uneven light. The ground is covered with a threadbare rug, its pattern faded but once fine. The air smells of lamp oil, canvas, and woodsmoke from the fire outside.

Read Aloud — The Attendees: The three nobles are already seated. Tichon Darelius stands behind his chair rather than sitting, his arms crossed, his steel-grey hair catching the lamplight. He wears a dark wool greatcoat over a high-collared tunic, his brass buttons dull but polished. Across from him, Lord Maxis Fontides sits with perfect posture, one hand resting on the table, his burgundy velvet coat immaculate, his silver-white hair oiled and swept back. He regards you with the faintest smile, as if you are an amusing distraction. At the far end, Duchess Aris Placidia sits with her ledger closed before her, her indigo silk gown the only color in the room, her silver-streaked hair braided tight. She watches you enter but says nothing.

Near the tent wall, apart from the nobles, Marcus Leondis stands in his patched leather cuirass, his tarnished brass badge catching the light. He nods once in your direction — a gesture of recognition, not deference.

Attendees:

Jace Valamacke — Host, Fleurite Exile leader — Liberate Fleurite from Inquisitors, free King Peter, peace treaty with Goodman exiles
Count Tichon Darelius — Steel Baron, Goodman camp co-leader — Separate settlement — Goodman exiles create their own
Lord Maxis Fontides — Mill Baron, Goodman camp co-leader — Dominant commerce sector in Fleurite, equal to the crown
Duchess Aris Placidia — Silk Baron, Goodman camp co-leader — Neutral — wants wealth/status back, leans alliance with Fleurite but distrusts them
Marcus Leondis — Goodman Militia commander — Wants dissolution of monarchy and oligarchy, favors Unity-style democracy (won't say this openly)
Vika Lana — Forest elf, independent — Wants to focus on the global Romulus problem
The Party — — — Unknown

Likely Flow:

1. Jace opens with the proposal: destroy the Inquisitors, free King Peter, negotiate peace.
2. Each noble stakes their position.
3. Marcus stays quiet unless drawn out.
4. Vika redirects toward the larger Romulus threat.
5. Party navigates between these factions.

Key Tensions:

Ruhrogue's identity as one of Goodman's assassins is unknown to the nobles. If revealed, it would disturb the peace.
The Goodman nobles assume the party are "poors" — reduces their perceived worth.
Fleurite exiles have only ~50 troops vs. ~150 Goodman militia. Jace has little leverage.
Jace has been stalling merger by exaggerating the party's importance from their mountain expedition.
The party's actual accomplishments exceed Jace's claims. If the party tells their own story well, it validates Jace's bluff. If they downplay it or fail to impress, Jace loses credibility.

What the Party Knows (From Legwork):

If the party did their legwork, they should have:
Aris's position — she's the most persuadable, but she needs to see a path to regaining her wealth.
Maxis's ambition — he wants power, not just survival. He can be bought with a position.
Tichon's stubbornness — he wants separation. He won't be moved easily.
Marcus's hidden sympathies — he's an ally in waiting, but he won't act openly.
The rations crisis — the camp can't sustain itself indefinitely. This is a lever.
The militia's weakness — the Goodman fighting force is fragile. Morale is low.

Contingencies:

If Ruhrogue's identity is revealed: Immediate crisis. The nobles may demand justice or attack. Aris may be the most likely to demand a trial rather than violence.
If the party brokers a deal: Determine what each faction is willing to concede.
If Jace's bluff is called: The nobles demand to know what the party actually accomplished. Low rolls on the party's recounting will weaken Jace's position. High rolls with the NPCs they've cultivated will strengthen it.
If the party ignores legwork: The nobles will be more dismissive. The party will have less to work with at the table.

Possible Outcomes:

Alliance: The camps unite under a joint command. The nobles accept Jace's proposal with conditions.
Separation: Tichon wins. The camps remain separate but agree to mutual defense.
Subjugation: Maxis wins. The Fleurite exiles become subservient to the Goodman nobles.
Stalemate: No agreement. The meeting ends with tensions higher than before.
Collapse: Ruhrogue's identity is revealed, or a deal is botched. The camps split violently.

Fleurite Castle is a major seat of power.

Fleurite Castle is a major seat of power within Fleurite. Romulus rules from the castle while controlling King Peter le Fleur and the Inquisition.

Romulus was practically born to enact the Infinite Twilight. He had visions of it for decades before the priesthood of Malygos brought him in on their plan. The Far Realm Entity selected him as a child (~290CE) to serve as its Controlled Anchor on Myrin.

Following the death of the hero Ruh at "The Ocho," Romulus used his psionic powers to mentally dominate King Peter le Fleur, effectively ending the benevolent monarchy. He rebranded the White Cloaks into the Inquisitors and synthesized the Church's religious authority with the capitalist greed of Goodman's former city-state to fund his global expansion.

Arrival:

Read Aloud — Outside: As the late afternoon light fades, you are called to the Goodman Administration Tent. It sits at the east edge of the camp, a massive pavilion of heavy canvas, its peak rising a full ten feet above the surrounding tents. Before it, a large communal firepit roars — more for ceremony than warmth, throwing long shadows across the trampled ground. A handful of armed militiamen stand at loose attention near the entrance, their eyes tracking you as you approach. The tent flaps are tied open, revealing a warm orange glow from within.

Read Aloud — Inside: The pavilion is spacious, the canvas walls braced with salvaged timber poles. A long table of dark, scarred wood dominates the center — heavy enough to have been a merchant's counter in another life. Mismatched chairs surround it: a high-backed armchair at the head, a few upholstered seats, the rest simple wooden stools. An oil lamp hangs from the center pole, casting a warm, uneven light. The ground is covered with a threadbare rug, its pattern faded but once fine. The air smells of lamp oil, canvas, and woodsmoke from the fire outside.

Read Aloud — The Attendees: The three nobles are already seated. Tichon Darelius stands behind his chair rather than sitting, his arms crossed, his steel-grey hair catching the lamplight. He wears a dark wool greatcoat over a high-collared tunic, his brass buttons dull but polished. Across from him, Lord Maxis Fontides sits with perfect posture, one hand resting on the table, his burgundy velvet coat immaculate, his silver-white hair oiled and swept back. He regards you with the faintest smile, as if you are an amusing distraction. At the far end, Duchess Aris Placidia sits with her ledger closed before her, her indigo silk gown the only color in the room, her silver-streaked hair braided tight. She watches you enter but says nothing.

Near the tent wall, apart from the nobles, Marcus Leondis stands in his patched leather cuirass, his tarnished brass badge catching the light. He nods once in your direction — a gesture of recognition, not deference.

The Dungeon Incursion:

A tall, slender elf with dark hair, Jace was introduced to the players by Vika Lana at the Dirty Duckling. He revealed that his wife, Lady Lily Valamacke, had been arrested and taken to the dungeon under Castle Fleurite just two days prior, expediting his need for action.

graph_sources.assertion:
Ruling Fleurite from the shadows of the throne. He seeks to use his new surge of leyline power to finalize the Infinite Twilight and expand the Inquisition's reach across all nations.

Three-Pronged Counterstrike (post-Monastery):

After the party's escape from the Monastery, Romulus initiated three moves in parallel:
1. Send Ishi'go'dan east — Commanded the Titan to fly to the island of Mythis Minor and destroy the castle at Tsunadis, opening the door for the cultists summoning Ragga'na'ken.
2. Crack down on Fleurite peasants — A vindictive show of force, burning outer districts.
3. Send troops to wipe out the exile encampment — A preemptive strike against the rebellion before it can rally.

The Inflection Point:

Romulus constructed a massive ley-energy focus in the treasure room of Fleurite Castle — a statue built from Aeon Stone material connected to all four elemental domains. It serves as the reflecting point for the Infinite Twilight. He pours psionic energy into it daily. Only the Inquisitors and a handful of artisans know about it.

Final Campaign (Pre-Assault):

Before the party's assault on Fleurite, Romulus becomes openly consumed by power and paranoia:
Orders the Exile Camp destroyed.
Begins mass executions in Fleurite.
Sends Ishi'go'dan to support the cult at Mythis.

The inflection point takes the form of a statue that symbolically represents the Far Realm Entity — a hideous, corrupted male/female angel with ghastly proportions and tentacles. Romulus tells his followers it represents Lord Malygos. It is being constructed in the treasure room of Fleurite Castle. Only the Inquisitors and a handful of artisans know about it; most of those artisans have been murdered or driven insane.

Dariferra was a hero of his village before leaving to seek his fortune. He was eventually captured by the rising Inquisition and taken to the White Kingdom. He was used as a test subject for Romulus's experimental aberrant psionics, surviving only because of his inherent mental resilience and the eventual intervention of the party and Arkin.

Romulus recovers Goodman’s broken body from the ruins of "The Ocho" and reanimates him as a Flesh Golem to maintain the city's economic machinery. In Fleurite, Romulus excommunicates "democracy lovers" and transforms the White Cloaks into the Inquisitors.

Arrest:

Lady Lily Valamacke was arrested by the White Cloaks approximately two days before the dungeon incursion (late December 2025). Unlike Dariferra, who had been held for nearly a month and severely brutalized, Lily was kept physically unharmed. She was taken not for information or punishment, but as bait — the Inquisitors intended to draw the rebellion into the open.

Dungeon Incursion:

During the party's tunnel incursion into Castle Fleurite's dungeon, Lily was held in a cell along the upper right stretch of the main horizontal hallway. Hearing the noise of the incursion, she began calling out to rally other prisoners. When the party arrived, she immediately asked about Jace, demanded prisoners be freed, and pushed for action.

Once freed, she helped free numerous other prisoners — both rebels and civilians. Her actions significantly accelerated the breakdown of dungeon control during the escape.

Post-Escape:

After escaping through the tunnel back to Grey House, Lily and Jace quickly pieced together that the incursion had been too easy — she had never been meant to disappear long-term. The Inquisitors wanted names, faces, and a single place to point at and call treason.

As the rebels fled Grey House, Ishi'go'dan was forced by Romulus to destroy the manor with a lightning bolt.

Exile Camp:

The rebellion fled south and joined the Goodman City survivors' encampment. Lily and Jace have been keeping the peace between the Fleurite exiles and the Goodman City exiles — a tentative arrangement. She spoke alongside Jace about possibly working together to fight back against the Inquisitors.
